q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT DISTINCT s1.beer, s1.price, s1.bar FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.bar = s2.bar GROUP BY s1.bar, s1.price, s1.beer HAVING s1.price = MIN(s2.price)

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 attempts to find the cheapest beer served in each bar, while Q2 tries to identify beers that are the cheapest in each bar by comparing prices with other beers served in the same bar.
counterexample_dsp: Consider a bar that serves three beers: A, B, and C. Beer A is the cheapest, followed by beer B, and then beer C. Q1 will correctly identify beer A as the cheapest beer in the bar. However, Q2 will incorrectly identify beer B as the cheapest beer in the bar, as it compares the price of beer B with the price of beer C, which is higher than beer B's price.
